scope_amendments.authorized_by: operator decision (2026-09-03, this session), taken after Task 2 reported the omission rather than working around it.
scope_amendments.reason: Task 2 declares EmbeddingJobId, CorpusGenerationId and TransitionBatchId. Every one of the domain's eighty-odd identities is declared by the file-local `domain_id!` macro in crates/vestrace-domain/src/id.rs, and EmbeddingSpaceId already lives there. The macro carries no `#[macro_export]`, so it cannot be used from the new embedding module, and this plan's own Task 2 file list omitted id.rs. The alternative was to hand-write three identity types inside crates/vestrace-domain/src/embedding/, which would have kept the letter of the frozen scope while splitting sibling identities across two files for no reason a reviewer could accept.
scope_amendments.consequence: Three `domain_id!` lines are added beside the existing EmbeddingSpaceId. No existing identity changes and the macro is not exported. This is the first amendment of P04 and it is recorded against the plan's own review checklist, which warned that a plan whose file lists are visibly incomplete is not ready: this omission is evidence for that warning rather than against it.

scope_amendments.authorized_by: operator decision (2026-09-03, this session): stop and complete the file lists across all twelve tasks rather than amend once per failing test.
scope_amendments.reason: Task 3 added three guarded tables and two guarded functions, and p03_upgrade_provisioning failed with 'only the exact P02 and P03 guarded tables may be re-owned'. That assertion is P03's own defence against an allowlist growing silently, so it was working; the defect was this plan's file lists. Rather than amend once per failing suite, the coupling was enumerated from the tree: every file that pins an exact guarded table or function set, every construction site of NormalizedRetrievalRequest (which Task 9 retypes), every reader or writer of memory_embeddings (which gains a generation), the route inventory and OpenAPI parity suites the Task 5 routes must satisfy, the composition roots and the wiring tests that assert them, and the fault harness Task 11 extends. Nothing was added because it merely mentions embedding: each path was matched on the exact identifier it is coupled by.
scope_amendments.consequence: The change scope grows from 53 to 85 paths. Several will not be edited at all, which costs nothing: an unused change-scope path is permitted, while a missing one stops the package. This is the third amendment on the third task, and it is evidence for the plan's own review checklist item 6, which warned that a plan whose file lists are visibly incomplete is not ready. The plan has not been independently reviewed; these are the findings a reviewer would have returned on paper.

scope_amendments.authorized_by: operator decision (2026-09-03, this session): build the connection admission policy publisher in P04.
scope_amendments.reason: Task 4 established, by searching the tree rather than carrying P03's note, that the connection admission policy has a vocabulary and a consumer but no producer. ConnectionAdmissionPolicy and its identity are declared in crates/vestrace-domain/src/models/admission.rs, and vestrace_try_admit_provider_dispatch refuses with 'provider dispatch admission policy is absent' -- but nothing writes connection_admission_policy_revisions or _heads: no route, no service, no repository, and no guarded SQL function. Six test files insert the rows with raw SQL as the guarded owner because there is no other way. Both Run-step and embedding dispatch are therefore unreachable in production, which blocks G0 rather than only this package. The publisher's natural homes are the P03 connection command, repository and route, none of which this plan listed.
scope_amendments.consequence: P04 adds the missing producer: a guarded compare-and-swap function in migration 0187, its two allowlist entries, an application command, a repository method, and one HTTP route, proved by provider_admission. This is P03 subject matter completed inside P04 under an explicit operator decision, and the evidence must say so rather than presenting it as P04's own design.

scope_amendments.authorized_by: operator decision (2026-09-03, this session): build the connection admission policy publisher in P04, whose third amendment authorises 'one HTTP route' in as many words. This amendment adds nothing beyond what that route mechanically requires, under the operator's standing instruction to complete the file lists rather than stop once per file.
scope_amendments.reason: A route in this codebase cannot exist outside crates/vestrace-http/src/route_inventory.rs: mount() asserts the descriptor is in the inventory and route_descriptor() panics when it is not, so an unlisted path is a startup panic rather than an undocumented route. Its served OpenAPI document is built by crates/vestrace-cli/src/commands/schema.rs, which is what crates/vestrace-cli/tests/provider_openapi_contract.rs -- already in scope since the second amendment -- reads through `vestrace schema http`. Neither file was listed, for the same reason the previous three amendments were needed.
scope_amendments.consequence: One governed inventory entry (POST /v1/connections/{id}/admission-policies, WorkspaceAdmin, Critical) and one OpenAPI path are added. No existing route, capability or risk classification changes.
scope_amendments.finding: schemas/openapi-v1.json, which this plan lists as the OpenAPI document to modify, is not the served schema and is read by nothing: it has not changed since the initial commit, carries 33 paths against the CLI document's full set, names only /v1/connections among the connection routes, and no test, build step or console module reads it. Adding a path there would look like documentation and verify nothing. The served document is the CLI's, and that is what this task modifies.

scope_amendments.authorized_by: This plan's own Task 4 interface, which states that `ProviderDispatchRepository` gains `load_embedding_dispatch_plan` and `recover_embedding_job_attempt`. That file is the only place those methods can be implemented, so the amendment adds nothing the task did not already require; it is recorded under the operator's standing instruction to complete the file lists rather than stop once per file.
scope_amendments.reason: PgProviderDispatchRepository is the single implementation of ProviderDispatchRepository and lives in this file. Rust permits one `impl Trait for Type` block, so the two new methods cannot be implemented anywhere else. The alternative -- a second Pg type implementing the same trait for embeddings -- is what Task 4 Step 4 asks a reviewer to confirm did not happen: it would end 'one dispatch authority, two callers' while leaving the trait looking shared. The plan listed embedding_job_repository.rs and postgres/mod.rs but not this file.
scope_amendments.consequence: Two methods and their row decoders are added beside their Run-step twins. No existing method, SQL statement or error mapping changes. The dirty-baseline verifier caught this before any test did, which is the contrast worth noting against the CRLF defect recorded in the evidence: the verifier pins the digest of every baseline dirty file, and says nothing about the shape of changes to files already inside the change scope.

scope_amendments.reason: Task 5 creates embedding_effect_recovery.rs, which needs the same governed fixture embedding_dispatch_is_atomic.rs already builds: a workspace, connection, revision, no-auth binding, model revision, qualification chain, binding snapshot, space registration, effect intent, accepted job, evidence root and admission policy. Rust test binaries share no code, so the alternatives were to duplicate roughly 250 lines or to add a shared module. scope_amendments.consequence: The fixture moves to crates/vestrace-infrastructure/tests/common/mod.rs and both suites include it with #[path]. No production code changes. If the operator prefers the frozen list, the fix is to duplicate the fixture in the new file and accept the drift risk.

scope_amendments.authorized_by: lead-engineer decision (2026-09-04, this session), taken after Task 5 investigation found the capability absent rather than assuming it existed.
scope_amendments.reason: Spec line 257 makes the acknowledgement an authorized command, and this package's only mechanism for authorizing a route is a Capability variant named by a route_inventory descriptor: `governed!` builds the AuthorizationRequest directly from it, so there is no way to gate the route without one. `Capability` has twenty-six variants and no embedding member, and both of its exhaustive match sites are in this file. Capabilities persist as free text with no closed-set database constraint, so nothing outside this file enumerates them. The alternative was to reuse an unrelated existing capability, which would have authorized the acknowledgement under a name that does not describe it.
scope_amendments.consequence: One variant, `EmbeddingRetryAfterUnknown`, with its Display and FromStr arms. The two transition-scoped capabilities line 257 also names are deliberately not added: they belong to Tasks 7 and 8, and adding them now would leave unused variants standing as if the routes existed. Those tasks need no further amendment, because this file is now in scope.

scope_amendments.authorized_by: lead-engineer decision (2026-09-04, this session), taken after Task 6 review ran the three provider suites the implementer had reported as inconclusive and found them failing rather than truncated.
scope_amendments.reason: Task 6 adds a deferrable constraint trigger making every model_binding_snapshots row require a durable scope row by commit time. That is a global invariant on a P03 table, and it correctly refuses the six test fixtures across three suites that insert a snapshot directly rather than through vestrace_create_run_model_binding_snapshot: 64 tests fail with 23514 'model binding snapshot requires a durable scope'. Two of those three suites are outside the P04 allowlist. The alternative was to weaken the invariant so the fixtures' shortcut keeps working, which would let test convenience decide production semantics — the opposite of what this package tells its implementer. The implementer's own report attributed these suites to a terminal problem ('detached overlapping cargo processes ... partial output') and did not count them; that attribution was wrong and the review re-ran them to establish it.
scope_amendments.consequence: Each affected fixture gains an INSERT into model_binding_snapshot_scopes beside its existing snapshot INSERT. No assertion, message comparison or expected count in either P03 suite may change; the amendment authorises additive fixture rows only. This is the first P04 amendment whose cause is a new invariant reaching beyond the package's own files, and it is recorded as such: a global constraint on a shared table is not a local change, however local its migration looks.
